_meta.description: Human-food grading hazard model for the P_human term. This is a STRUCTURED EXPERT MODEL, not a trained classifier, and the API labels it as such. No French open dataset records per-lot grading outcomes, so there is no label to train on; inventing one would make a fabricated number look like a measurement.
_meta.form: P_human = base(crop) * PRODUCT(1 - penalty_i), clipped, where each penalty is a documented agronomic mechanism driven by a real weather feature.
_meta.calibration: NOT CALIBRATED against any measurement, and an earlier version of this file wrongly claimed it was ('set so the long-run human-grade share matches published market balances'). That claim was checked and could not be substantiated: no market-balance series exists in this repository and nothing pins these values to one. base(crop) is ordered expert judgement - lentil and chickpea above pea and fava bean, because whole visible seed is graded more strictly - and the slopes, caps and crop_sensitivity multipliers below are the same. The MECHANISMS are real published agronomy; their coefficients are not measured. Treat every number in this file as a prior.
_meta.replace_with: Per-lot grading records from a cooperative silo would turn this into a genuinely trained classifier. That is the single highest-value dataset a partner could contribute.
_meta.why_a_false_provenance_claim_was_worse_t: A number with no stated source invites a reader to discount it. A number with a source it does not have invites them to trust it, and then to discount everything else in the project when they check. The engine already reports this block with provenance mode 'reference_table' and the API states it has no observational labels; the _meta now matches that rather than contradicting it.

harvest_staining.mechanism: July rain on mature pods causes fungal staining and seed discolouration, the dominant reason lots are refused for retail packing.

bruchid_damage.mechanism: Bruchus beetles begin laying eggs on young pods once daily maxima pass about 20 C. Larval exit holes above the 2 percent tolerance downgrade the lot.

drought_splitting.mechanism: A dry grain-fill followed by rewetting at harvest splits seed coats and shrivels grain, pushing calibre below food specification.

heat_abortion_smallseed.mechanism: Heat during flowering aborts flowers and leaves a high share of small, light seed that fails calibre screening even when total yield looks acceptable.

no_optical_sorting_access.mechanism: Without optical sorting within haulage range, a lot cannot be cleaned to retail insect-damage and discolouration tolerances, so a marginal lot goes to feed instead of being sorted into a passing fraction.

fraction_distribution.description: A harvest is not simply pass or fail. Part of a lot can be sorted into a passing fraction while the rest goes to feed, so the engine samples a human-grade FRACTION rather than flipping a single coin. Treating it as one coin flip per harvest overstates the spread of farm income; treating it as a fixed expectation understates the downside.
fraction_distribution.form: Beta(a, b) with mean = P_human and concentration kappa, plus an independent catastrophic-downgrade event.

catastrophic_downgrade.description: Whole-lot rejection: mycotoxin, a failed residue test, or staining so severe no sorting recovers it. Independent of the graded fraction.

protein_response.description: Protein concentration moves inversely with yield (the dilution effect), which is why a drought year can fail a calibre specification while passing a protein specification.
